To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

serum levels of CEA, total sialic acids and total phosphohexoseisomerase are significantly higher in untreated lung cancer cases compared to the controls and that the levels of these markers are higher in non- responding cases as compared to the responders.
TSA/TP, a marker of cell membrane turnover, and PHI, a glycolytic enzyme, are superior to CEA in the diagnosis of lung cancer and are useful in predicting the outcome of treatment.
TSA/TP is a better tumor marker than CEA for the detection of lung cancer and that the combination of TSA/TP, PHI and CEA can improve the detection of lung cancers in the future.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new markers and to develop a new strategy for the early diagnosis, treatment and monitoring of lung cancer patients.
the identification of quantifiable serum tumor markers for the early detection and follow-up of lung cancer patients.
the identification of quantifiable tumor biomarkers as adjuncts to the clinical care of patients with lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TSA/TP is a better tumor marker than CEA and PHI for lung cancer patients.
the combination of CEA, PHI and TSA/TP may be used as an effective tool for screening and diagnosis of lung cancer.
TSA/TP is the best tumor marker for lung cancer patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CEA has limited value in the diagnosis of lung cancer.
the serum levels of total sialic acids and phosphohexoses isomerase are better tumor markers than C.E.A. in lung cancer patients.
the TSA/TP ratio and serum levels of PHI may be useful in the diagnosis of lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TSA/TP ratio and PHI are better tumor markers than CCEA in patients with lung cancer.
the combination of TSA/TP with CEA or PHI can be used as a better diagnostic tool than CEA or TSA/TP alone.
TSA/TP ratio and PHI are more reliable markers of lung cancer than CEA and can be used as adjuncts to improve the accuracy of diagnosis of lung cancer.
